title: Julie & Julia
tagline: One cookbook. One year. One very good stew.
about: A frustrated writer cooks her way through a classic French cookbook, interwoven with the story of the cook who wrote it.
cue: Serve the mains when Julie finally nails the boeuf bourguignon.
faces: Where it all began: a lunch in Rouen, a cooking class full of men in white, and a mountain of onions.
Whole sole dusted in flour, browned in butter, lemon, parsley.
Rouen, the first lunch. Paul ordered.
Warm Gruyère choux puffs, a grating of nutmeg.
Chocolate almond cake, soft middle, dark chocolate glaze.
The Queen of Sheba. A cake from the book.
Julia at the fish market. The sole, 70 francs the kilo.
Our kitchen table, and the Queen of Sheba, going fast.
Everything tonight comes out of Julia's book, cooked in a kitchen the size of a closet. The beef is attempt two. I fell asleep on attempt one.
Did the lobsters make it? I check this blog before my email.
AT JULIE'S, ABOVE THE PIZZA PLACE
Dry white Burgundy poured over crème de cassis, a blackberry.
Toasted ciabatta rubbed with garlic, ripe tomato, basil, olive oil.
Two live lobsters, boiled, lemon and drawn butter.
Beef braised in red wine, bacon, carrots, onions, mushrooms.
Attempt number two. Nobody fell asleep.
Whole duck, boned, stuffed with pork and veal, in pastry.
Boned by hand. It took a while.
Prices are the grocery bill. No Cobb salad.

    StartersJulie's bruschettaToasted ciabatta rubbed with garlic, ripe tomato, basil, olive oil.What I make when the day was long. $5.24.How to make it1 ciabatta, sliced1 garlic clove, halved4 ripe tomatoes1 small bunch basil, torn2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil1/2 tsp saltDice the tomatoes, salt them and leave 10 minutes (included in cook time).Toast the ciabatta slices and rub with the cut garlic.Mix the tomatoes with basil and oil and pile on just before serving.GougèresWarm Gruyère choux puffs, a grating of nutmeg.Practice for the cooking school.How to make it125ml water50g butter75g plain flour2 eggs80g gruyere, grated1/4 tsp ground nutmegBoil the water with the butter, beat in the flour and cook for a minute.Cool slightly, beat in the eggs one at a time, then the gruyere and nutmeg.Pipe small rounds onto lined trays.Bake at 200°C until puffed and golden. Bon appetit.MainsBoeuf bourguignonBeef braised in red wine, bacon, carrots, onions, mushrooms.Attempt number two. Nobody fell asleep.How to make it1.2kg beef chuck, diced150g bacon lardons2 carrots, sliced1 brown onion, diced2 garlic cloves750ml red wine250ml beef stock2 thyme sprigs of and 2 bay leaves12 pearl onions, peeled250g mushrooms40g butterDry the beef and brown it in batches with the lardons.Soften the carrots, onion and garlic in the same pot.Return the meat, add the wine, stock, thyme and bay leaves and bring to a simmer.Braise covered at 160°C for 3 hours until the beef is tender.Glaze the pearl onions and mushrooms in the butter and stir through at the end.SweetsReine de SabaChocolate almond cake, soft middle, dark chocolate glaze.The Queen of Sheba. A cake from the book.How to make it185g dark chocolate120g butter3 eggs, separated100g caster sugar60g almond meal30g plain flourMelt most of the chocolate with most of the butter and cool a little.Separate the eggs and beat the yolks with the sugar, add the chocolate, then fold in the almond meal and flour.Whip the whites and fold in.Bake in a lined tin at 180°C, then cool.Melt the remaining chocolate with the remaining butter and glaze the cake.DrinksKirDry white Burgundy poured over crème de cassis, a blackberry.Day 1 of 365. $3.65.How to make it750ml dry white Burgundy or chardonnay60ml creme de cassis4 blackberriesChill the bottle for 2 hours (included in cook time).Pour the cassis into wine glasses, top slowly with the cold Burgundy or chardonnay so it blends from the bottom, and drop a blackberry in each. Serve before the bourguignon.
